title: O My Son Absalom
reflectionText: Every runner came with the same word — the battle won, the enemy scattered, all well. The king heard none of it. He asked one thing, and asked it twice: not whether the war was won, but whether the young man was safe. What remains of a victory bought with your own son?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-24, Batch C (gap G7). 2 Samuel 18, the death of Absalom and David's grief, absent both lanes. SHORT + FULL only (owner-locked; no long variant). WEB 333/651w, KJV 346/710w. David's grief carried by the passage's own words (18:33) with no added sentiment or melodrama; the king's threefold 'deal gently' charge (18:5), the repeated single question 'Is it well with the young man Absalom?' (18:29, 18:32), and Joab's disobedience are kept. Ends on the terminal grief of 18:33 ('would God I had died for thee'); no material after the cry. No motive or commentary added beyond the source.
